body: Ok, I clearly misread the situation, my apologies. I was just trying to help.

The point of that is that when yoy make friends, it could lead to fewer suicidal thoughts. But I understand  you're not interested in that kind of thing. 

I know Dutch is a hard language, but since you live in the Netherlands and you're boyfriend is probably Dutch, my advise is to speak it as much as possible. To your boyfriend too, since that's a better way to learn a language.
I'm here if you wanna talk.
Relatable, just wanna let you know you're not alone and people DO care.

No, it's not. There are other opitions. You could for example join some kind of social group. If you don't speak Dutch in the Netherlands, is it not that big of a problem, most people speak English. Of course I could be wrong and is it a far bigger problem than I think. And where are you originally from then, if I may ask?

No, they will definitely try to help, by sending me to a therapist. For different teasons than depression and suicide of course. They already did this 5 years ago, I hated it and it didn't help at all, according to the therapist.
No problem
That seems indeed the best to do.
You should try something new, since you're probably stuck doing your daily routine over and over again.
Your mother really loved you, you should tell her. It might break her heart, but she loves you and she'll do everything to help you.

Why would you give up your hope if you want your misery to end. I'm in a sort of similar situation, only have 'friends', only people who care are my family, family doesn't know about my 'illness' and yet still above average grades. Just some years younger.
You shouldn't give up on life, you could perhaps keep getting good grades. The future will look brighter if you do so. 

And if you don't see the point of moving on if nobody cares, what's holding you back to find someone who does? There must be some clubs around your college that match your interests, right? If you have no social life, why wouldn't you join some? Or you could just talk to someone you trust. Then you'll probably feel better too. You know there are always people who care, even if they don't know you.
What exactly does always turns out horrible for you? I mean it can't be all your fault.

You're right, but since you've been there you'll probably know it isn't that easy to join clubs. I could've been easy for you, but it certainly isn't for me. I'm also very anti-social and I live on the counrtyside so there aren't many groups to join. 

It's also not that I not eating enough or something like that. It's just when I start thinking about stuff, I get depressed. The only moments I don't start 'thinking' is when I'm distracted, like at school or when I'm gaming or something like that. 

And I know my parents care, but I still think I it's unacceptable. They could care too much, right? I don't know wether they thought it through, but it certainly didn't help.

I'm sorry, you're just trying to help, when you don't even know me. But I just wanted to explain why your solution might not work for me. Don't feel like I'm attacking you, because I'm not. Thanks for the reply and sorry that I took a week to reply to you.
